r7-close-criteria.title: Close criteria C2-C6
r7-close-criteria.imperative: Verify each named close criterion (C2 single seam set, C3 both directions, C4 adversarial non-omission fixture, C5 #308 not precluded, C6 never half-retired) against the code and by independent reproduction.
r7-close-criteria.finding: C2 MET (verified by grep and by mutation). C3 MET (both directions, in-process and through real CLI subprocesses; retired episode absent from ordinary retrieval, present history-inclusively, still fetchable by id). C5 MET (19 tests; cluster survivors stay findable, retired member reachable three ways). C4 UNMET: the adversarial fixtures prove the three NAMED traps are closed, but retrieval DOES silently omit / hard-refuse on the shipped store itself - the deliverable's own episodes/active/README.md and episodes/retired/README.md make every scanning primitive and the writer refuse. C6 PARTLY MET: unrepresentable-by-construction and compensated-rollback both verified sound; the third layer (loud on the residual) does not hold for fetch-by-id or for the writer's retire op.

r8-fourth-trap.title: Hunt a fourth relocated silent-omission trap
r8-fourth-trap.imperative: Verify the three claimed fixtures catch what they claim (mutation-substitute a naive impl), then hunt a fourth: case-insensitive FS, missing directory, file in BOTH dirs, symlinks, id colliding with a non-episode filename, dotfiles, nested subdirs, unicode/normalization.
r8-fourth-trap.finding: FOURTH TRAP FOUND AND DEMONSTRATED (blocker). NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES is enforced ONLY at the flat store root (stray_episode_paths globs root/*.md); it is never applied inside active/ or retired/, which iter_episode_ids globs unconditionally. The gate's own shipped placeholders episodes/active/README.md + episodes/retired/README.md therefore yield stems {README} in BOTH sets, so _reject_half_retired fires on the REAL tracked store: 'python scripts/query_episodes.py enumerate' exits 1 with 'half-retired store: README exists in BOTH active/ and retired/'. select/neighbours/enumerate --include-retired and the writer's create all refuse identically. With only one README present the store yields a PHANTOM id 'README' from enumerate_episode_ids and then dies 'corrupt episode: missing episode-state header'. Separately verified: the three claimed traps DO have teeth (7 independent source mutations, all red). Additional lesser traps: a missing/absent active/ dir reads as an empty store with no refusal; nested-subdir strays (episodes/archive/x.md, episodes/active/old/x.md) are silently omitted; fetch/resolve_episode_path silently pick the active copy in a half-retired store.

r9-half-retirement.title: Half-retirement live probe (C6 layer 3)
r9-half-retirement.imperative: Create an episode present in BOTH active/ and retired/ and confirm readers AND the writer refuse rather than silently picking one. Also probe rollback on injected faults.
r9-half-retirement.finding: Readers that SCAN refuse correctly (enumerate/select/neighbours, both directions) and writer create refuses. But (a) fetch_episode/resolve_episode_path silently return the active/ copy - resolve_episode_path's docstring asserts 'an episode is never in both places at once', false in exactly the residual state the design admits; (b) writer 'retire' and any op that does not trigger an id-assignment scan PROCEED against a half-retired store. docs section 7 and g4-result claim the state is 'refused by readers and by the writer alike' - over-claimed. Rollback layers (a) and (b) verified sound.

r10-nonepisode.title: NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES mechanism ruling
r10-nonepisode.imperative: Judge whether the filename allowlist is the right mechanism or reintroduces the same drift shape as the character-list guard this run already replaced once.
r10-nonepisode.finding: RULING: the named-allowlist PRINCIPLE is right and load-bearing (mutation M6, emptying NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES, turns 4 tests red - the exclusion really is coming from the allowlist and not from a glob shape). But the MECHANISM reintroduces the same drift shape as the character-list guard, in two ways. (1) SCOPE DRIFT, already realised: the allowlist is consulted at exactly one of the three directories that now hold files - the flat root - and never inside active/ or retired/. Membership moved from content to location, but the non-episode classifier did not move with it. That asymmetry IS the blocker. (2) HAND-MAINTAINED ENUMERATION standing in for a computable property: the store already owns an id grammar (kebab-case run + '-' + three digits, enforced at create and relied on by _next_episode_id's suffix.isdigit()). 'Is this filename an episode?' is derivable from that grammar; a frozenset of filenames must be edited every time anyone adds a .gitkeep, a CODEOWNERS, an index.md or a second README variant, and forgetting is silent in one direction and store-bricking in the other. RECOMMENDATION: make the id grammar the classifier applied uniformly in all three directories (a *.md file whose stem is not a well-formed episode id is a non-episode; refuse it as misfiled if it sits in active/ or retired/, ignore it at the flat root only if named in a small allowlist). That is drift-free by construction and would have refused the shipped placeholders at authoring time instead of at first use.

r11-docs.title: Doc accuracy (EPISODE_STORE.md 7/8/9/10)
r11-docs.imperative: Verify §7 describes what shipped, §§8/10 match reality, §9's identical-file-content claim is corrected, and Option B survives as rejected-with-reason.
r11-docs.finding: Section 7 describes what shipped (ruling quoted verbatim, Option A bound, Option B retained as rejected-with-reason with its real advantage and real cost stated, seam table filled with bound implementations, the three relocated traps named). Sections 8 and 10 now match reality; I checked every primitive and CLI flag section 8 claims. Section 9's 'identical file content' is correctly replaced by 'the same content at the same blob OID' with a new paragraph naming .gitattributes '* text=auto', the platform conversion, the pinning test, and issue #319 - doc and test now agree. Sections 1/2/3 swept of the stale Option-B disclaimers.
